correctness.rationale: The pole edge forbids a face containing both poles. Deleting them yields a join X of Ind(P_{ell_i-1}); the two pole cones have bases Y_u,Y_v which are joins of Ind(P_{ell_i-2}), with the actual inclusions into X. The path formula follows by folding vertex 3 onto vertex 1 (its open neighborhood contains that of vertex 1), leaving P_2 disjoint from P_{n-3}, and treating P_0,P_1,P_2 explicitly. Thus X is contractible exactly when some length has residue 2, and the bases are contractible exactly when some length has residue 0; each noncontractible join has formal sphere dimension R-1. For all lengths 1 mod 3, the path endpoint inclusion is obtained by attaching a cone on the contractible Ind(P_{3a-2}); gluing along this subcomplex gives a homotopy equivalence, and joins preserve it. The first pole cone then leaves a contractible space and the second gives S^R. With a residue-0 arm both bases are contractible so the cones preserve X. In the remaining case, X is contractible, hence both maps through it are null, and the two cones yield the wedge of two S^R. If all arms have length 2 the join-unit convention means the bases have empty realization; the interior simplex and two isolated poles give exactly three components. This is an all-parameter homotopy proof, not a Betti-number extrapolation.
residual_risks: The independent replay checks reduced Euler characteristic in the listed 70 instances; the frozen mod-2 Betti check was inspected, not run. Neither finite check proves integral homotopy; that conclusion comes from the cone argument.

value.rationale: This classifies a natural generalization of the theta graph at the level of homotopy, not merely homology. Both the collapse to a point when residues 0 and 2 mix and the sharp two-summand limit, independent of how many arms occur, are useful distinctions. The exact pole-attachment test explains why adding arbitrarily many routes does not create higher wedge multiplicities.
residual_risks: Limited to the direct-edge, internally disjoint model; no claim about unspined graphs or equivariant or simple-homotopy type.
